**Surah al-Tin (The Fig). Its central theme:**

[The secret] central theme of ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1] is the establishment of complete power, which is indicated by its name. In the creation of the fig and the olive there are marvels that point to this. Likewise, in what is indicated by them of the prophetic missions, and in the joining of the oath to what it is sworn upon, which is man, who is the most wondrous thing in the universe, [it is] evident in this: "In the name of God" (the Sovereign, the Greatest, whom we worship only), "the Compassionate" (whose grace encompasses the bringing into existence and the clarifying of all His creation, the lowest, the highest, the nearest, and the farthest), "the Merciful" (who singled out from among them the people of His love with what He is pleased with, and abased and wretched those who opposed them).

When Glory and Exaltation be to Him had mentioned in that surah the most perfect of His creation and what He perfected him with, and concluded it with the command to single out Him, Glory and Exaltation be to Him, with the turning of desire toward Him, the Prophet (ﷺ) would stand [in prayer] until his feet swelled and would exert effort for his Lord in everything that pleases Him. In this surah He mentioned that, just as He made His essence the most perfect of created essences, He singled him (ﷺ) out by making his kind the most perfect of kinds, which is man, and his origin the greatest of origins, which is Abraham (ﷺ), and his land the best of lands, which is Makkah. [He mentioned] that whoever opposes him by rejecting his law is the lowest of creation, and that He, Glory and Exaltation be to Him, has complete power and acts by choice, exalting whom He wills and lowering whom He wills. Thus its position relative to the end of that surah is the position of the cause relative to the effect. In it He swore by things, indicating through them their nobility in themselves and in their wondrous making, and the nobility of the places in which they occur, as an allusion to what He honored them with, of goodness and blessings that He manifested through them, by the dwelling of the Prophets, the blessings and peace of God be upon them all, and the righteous, the good pleasure of God be upon them all. Thus they were the emigration place of Abraham, the birthplace of Jesus, and the place of origin of most of the Prophets, peace be upon them. From it was the manifestation of the prophethood of Moses, and the manifestation of the prophethood of Isma'il, peace be upon them both, and of his descendant, the Seal of the Noble Prophets, upon him be the best of blessings and peace, and the site of the House which is ﴿a place of standing for mankind and guidance for the worlds﴾, along with other clear indications and manifest proofs of His complete power and His acting by choice, since He exalts whom He wills from among the rational beings and others, and from among places and others, in the best form, and lowers whom He wills from all of that to the lowest of the low.

Ibn al-Zubayr, Abu Ja'far, said: This surah clarifies and completes the theme of the two surahs before it. It becomes clear to you that the human form, by outward appearance, given the order and perfection that it has, would seem to require agreement, through the outward connection of perfection with it, in that He is a God who created in the best form, while separation seems remote outwardly. So how did judgment diverge and conduct differ? Whoever ascends through clarity and obedience, and whoever descends to the lowest of the low, not to mention the rising of some to degrees of perfection? Accordingly, only one who is singled out with the distinction of nearness rises, because he was called from near, so he hastened to answer his caller and listened attentively, and was not hindered by the one who drove him. So ask of the clear paths what was drawn for him, and what his deeds built upon what was written for him of that. ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13]. So it is incumbent upon the rational, fair person, regarding himself, to know that each is facilitated for what he was created for, and so he humbles himself before his Creator, seeking sincerity. «Whoever finds good, let him praise God.» This surah made clear that what God gave His Prophet (ﷺ), and singled him out with, of kinds of honors, and began him with great favors of the two surahs, along with what He granted him of the good of both abodes, and what it contains. [Among it is] His oath to him, Glory and Exaltation be to Him, that He has neither bidden him farewell nor forsaken him, of tenderness, companionship, and signs of love and nearness. All of that is grace from Him, Glory and Exaltation be to Him, and kindness, not for a prior deed (p-133) that would necessitate that or part of it. Even if a deed had preceded, it would not have occurred except by His will, His enabling, and His determination, and no one merits anything from Him. It is only His grace, which He gives to whom He wills. So Glory and Exaltation be to Him said, alerting to what the allusion had pointed to in part: ﴿Certainly We created man in the best form﴾ [al-Tin: 4]. Yet despite this, the outward form's existence in the world of witness, in the most perfect creation and the most complete arrangement, does not benefit him, rather, if it is not accompanied by enabling and is preceded by no happiness from his Creator, and no light is given to him by which he walks, he sees nothing but himself and knows only those of his kind. So his sight stops at the first thing he witnesses, and he halts at what he beholds without any habit that would lead him to realize his end and the clarity of his dwelling, that he was not a thing worth mentioning. So when he looks short and does not see, he believes himself to be perfect, and becomes blind to his beginning and his end. Thus he becomes the lowest of the low, since his sight is not benefited by the signs, nor does he know the reality of his own report: ﴿Has man not seen that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77] ﴿And he presents to Us a parable and forgets his creation﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78]. Then the Exalted said: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Tin: 6]. They are those whom their Lord guided ﴿by their faith﴾ [Yunus: 9], so they proceeded through Him in the best form among His creation, and clarified the straight path, and were given insight and so they saw, and they reflected and so took lesson. And they said: "Our Lord is God," then they were steadfast, so for them is a reward never cut off [end].

(p-134)

* *

Since the fig is, according to what they mentioned of its excellence, the best of fruits in form, and it is, along with being a very delicious sweet fruit, a food that strengthens the spine, a staple like wheat, quick to digest, and a remedy of great benefit that produces good blood, benefits the lungs and kidneys, softens the nature, dissolves phlegm, removes sand from the bladder, and opens the obstructions of the liver and spleen, it thus combined all the benefits of things consumed, as food, as fruit, as sweet, and as medicine. So it is perfect in the totality of what it is, of the pleasure of its taste and the abundance of its benefit, and in being like the fruit of Paradise, without any defect that hinders eating it, such as a cluster that wearies or a pit that must be discarded. Along with that, it is beneficial both fresh and dried. Yet despite this, in the speed of its spoiling and the badness of its change, it is the lowest in rank and the worst in outcome. So it is like the original nature at its beginning in ease, goodness, and acceptance of both improvement and change, like the end of old age at its conclusion in its great change, such that one benefits from none of it once it has changed. Other fruits, when one part spoils, another part remains. So in this it was like the portion for the lowest of mankind, by which God swore, saying: ﴿And the fig﴾, beginning with it because the oath indicated by it is greater in number, so attention to it is greater.

And since the olive is free from a spoilage that might touch it or a change that might reach it, and it contains richness, pungency, and bitterness, and it is both condiment and medicine, while being ready for benefit in every state, whether eaten after being pressed, or lit with its oil, or anointed with it to remove dishevelment, smooth the skin, strengthen the bone, and tighten the sinew, and other benefits, along with its tenderness and what follows from its many virtues, it is like the believer, [which He followed] by mentioning it, saying: ﴿And the olive﴾.

Since this, along with that, was indicated by the two [the fig and the olive] to the places where they grow, which is the Holy Land, meaning all the lands of al-Sham, as an allusion to the prophets who lived there and to those who followed them in goodness, especially Ibrahim (upon him be peace), whose place of migration it was. God the Exalted revived it through His servants, and the angels frequented it with revelation. After him came his offspring, whom God purified through them from shirk (associating partners with God) and illuminated through them with tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness). He concluded them with ʿIsa (upon him be peace), one of the ulu al-ʿazm (the resolute messengers), honored by being of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and upon our Prophet be the most excellent prayers and peace. The allusion to the land through the two trees, meaning its inhabitants, was more eloquent than explicit mention of the intended meaning at the outset. He drove the discourse along this noble method. Of their noble men, none who dwelt there remained except Musa, Harun, Isma'il and Muhammad (upon them be peace). He pointed to the first two with His saying, expressing it in a way that indicates the best stature, because the Tur is the mountain bearing vegetation of palms, fruit-bearing trees and other growth: ﴿And Mount [Sinai]﴾, meaning the mountain of the place known by this name.

Since the discourse concerned stature, the fitting form for it was the sound plural, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Sinin﴾, meaning and by what was on the mountain of good vegetation where God spoke to Musa (upon him be peace), with its sweet intimate conversation, wondrous promises and wise speech. Along with this, it contains trees and places that protect from heat and cold. In it, by its emptiness, beauty and loftiness, there is gathering of the heart for one who seeks solitude, and tranquility of the soul for withdrawing to worship and seeking protection from what is feared because of its height and difficulty. In it is what is fit for cultivation without hardship, and in it is what people and animals eat, along with sweet water, a spacious courtyard and a graceful view. Sinin and Sayna' are names for the place where this mountain is. He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, pointed to the last two of Ibrahim's offspring (upon him be peace) as a conclusion to the oath, by the most perfect of what is sworn by, just as He made the one revealed to him, who is the seal of the messengers, the most perfect of the kind sworn for. Thus at the beginning there is what follows good stature toward corruption, and the conclusion is with what is the most noble of those mentioned in every respect, a correspondence that attained the highest secrets.

(p-137) ﴿وهذا البلد﴾, that is, Makkah. Here he explicitly names these two places as a *tarshih* (a device, glossed here as "a sustaining complement" that reinforces what precedes) because what is meant by the first two are the places where the two fruits grow, together with the subtle allusion, by mentioning their names, to their suitability for the thing sworn by. ﴿الأمين﴾ [that is], the secure, in which whoever dwells among humans, birds and beasts is safe. It is thus like the trustworthy man whom another entrusts with his own self and what is dear to him, so he delivers it to him and honors him in regard to it. Its security encompasses everything that one fears, even poverty, destitution, hunger, and the alteration of the religion after its establishment. Moreover, in it is the House which God made "a guidance for the worlds" and "a standing place for the people," so it is the focal point of religion and of the world. It contains, through revelation and its traces, secrets that no other land possesses. This is an indication that, just as He, exalted is He, placed the Prophet sent from it at [the end of] time in the best of stature, He placed it in the best stature among the lands, since it was secure without a dreaded king, while people were being snatched away all around it. It is the place of intimacy with people, just as the one before it is the place of intimacy through solitude. It is the gathering place of amenities, the mine of benefits, and the seat of those held in esteem in religion and in worldly affairs, and the place of elevation and high positions. Along with this, the two places have received the descent of the heavenly scriptures and the radiance of the divine religious lights within them. In this there is a warning [to them] that if they do not turn back from their error, He will make him fear with a fear that He has not made any land of the lands of the Arabs fear. (p-138) Thus they will have been returned, in regard to the land, to "the lowest of the low," just as they have been returned, in morals, to schism and obstinate enmity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 95, verse 4:

Since this oath, together with its being comprehensive of the marvels of created things, which by [what has been mentioned of] their judgment indicate the perfection of their Creator's knowledge and the completeness of His power, and together with its being comprehensive of most of those who believed, and since Ibrahim, peace be upon him, being their father, was mentioned twice in relation to the holy land, from al-Quds (Jerusalem) and Makkah, the addressee of this mentioned oath, the most complete and most discerning of creation, anticipates [the answer]. Knowing that the oath has reached its goal and attained its utmost end, [the answer] is given by His words, exalted is He, affirming: ﴿Indeed, We created﴾, that is, We decreed and brought into being, by the dazzling greatness and the overpowering, dominating might that belong to Us, ﴿man﴾, that is, this kind in which He combined appetite and intellect, and in which is a self-attachment that makes him forget most of his important concerns. For this reason the angels, peace be upon them, said:

﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], because they knew that when anger and appetite are combined with intellect, dispute comes, so corruption arises from appetite and bloodshed from anger. ﴿In the best of forms﴾, that is, existing from Us as spirit and intellect, or more general than that, by what We made for him of good creation and good character, (p. 139) and by what He singled him out with, namely upright stature, beauty of form, and the gathering of the special qualities of beings and the counterparts of all possible things, after he shared with others the hearing, sight, taste, touch and smell, the organs which prepared him for what he was created for. Thus it was said that he is the lesser world (microcosm), as the exposition of this has passed in the commentary on surah al-Shams. Then We distinguished him by what We deposited in him, by the primordial nature (fitrah) that We placed upon him, which has no alteration, from the first sound disposition which We prepared for him and strengthened by Our power to accept the truth. In the same manner as what I have said regarding interpreting the verse as referring to the primordial nature, al-Asfahani said in his tafsir on ﴿Mankind were one community﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213] in al-Baqarah. [And] Ibn Burjan said here: he is created upon the fitrah of Islam, the upright religion. Then, when We granted him, with it, the upright perceiving intellect, just as We made for him a form that distinguishes him from the rest of the animals, so We granted him an intellect which guides him to ascend from the degree of the fires to the ranks of the Gardens, through faith and righteous deeds that reach the utmost limit of excellence, as evidenced by those among his [descendants] who are prophets, the most perfect of whom [is Muhammad] — upon all of them be the best of blessings, peace, greetings and honour — and by those who follow them in goodness, who filled the earth with knowledge, wisdom and light. Al-Baghawi said: He, glorified and exalted, created him tall of stature, taking his food with his hand, adorned (p. 140) with intellect and discernment, — end of quote. Intellect is in reality the intended thing in man, because among its names is lubb (kernel, core), and it is known that what is intended from [every] thing is its core, which is the Law, as has passed at the end of surah al-Nisa'. It is apparent that the intellects of people, by their creation, are close to one another, and [that] they only differ according to innate disposition. Some of them, glorified and exalted is He, made their origin and innate disposition in the extreme of corruption, so their disposition continues to ruin their intellect, and it diminishes until it reaches the worst of states. Each is made easy for what he was created for. Some of them turn their intellect, according to what Allah has prepared for it, toward what saves them, and some turn it, for that purpose, toward what destroys them. For you find the most intelligent of people in one matter and the most knowledgeable of it, while being the most dull in another matter, and the most ignorant in one thing being the most clever in another. So reflect on this. By this the affairs of creation are arranged in their livelihood through sciences, crafts and conditions. And Allah is the Guide.

This verse indicates that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is far removed from composition and form, for if He were in any of these two, He would be the most excellent, because every attribute shared by the created and the Truth [i.e., Allah], the superlative is for the Truth, like ʿālim (knowing) and aʿlam (more knowing), karīm (generous) and akram (most generous). This was said by Ustadh Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri in his tafsir. The form "afʿal" (more/most X) does not indicate what the Zanadiqa (heretics) said, even if that is attributed to some of the great scholars from their saying: "There is no possibility more wondrous than what has been." For the single degree differs into what cannot be enclosed by counting, like the differences among individual human beings in their forms and colours, and other than that of their existences and the wondrous nature of their affairs. I have explained this in a separate composition on this phrase, which I named: "Tahdim al-Arkan man 'Laysa fi al-Imkan Abda' mimma Kan'" (The Demolition of the Pillars of Those Who Say "There is no possibility more wondrous than what has been"), [and I made it fully clear and explained, and trials arose in it that deafen the ears, and Allah supported the truth by the agreement of the notables, and subdued the people of tyranny. Then I followed it with the book "Dalalat al-Burhan ʿala anna fi al-Imkan Abda' mimma Kan" (The Proof of the Argument That There Is in Possibility Something More Wondrous Than What Has Been)], then the diseases were healed, the adversaries were humiliated, the illusions were repelled, by the statement that distinguishes the truthful from the hypocrite, which is about two leaves in extreme originality in ending disputes. It is possible that the form afʿal is meaningful [in relation] to something Allah intended, such that we might perceive it [ourselves], because among what is agreed upon by the People of the Sunnah, and stated by al-Ash'ari and others in more than one place in their books, is that Allah, exalted is He, His capabilities have no end. Among those who stated what al-Ash'ari stated and elaborated upon is the Proof of Islam, Imam al-Ghazali, in his books, al-Ihya' and others, especially his book "Tahafut al-Falasifa" (The Incoherence of the Philosophers), and he made clear that this is among their principles for negating the attribute of will and their saying that His act is by essence, and he made clear the corruption of that, (p. 142) and that He, glorified and exalted is He, is able to originate another [world] and a third, differing in smallness and greatness, and upon every possible thing. He knew that the possible is what is capable of being done, and that what returns to the capable is also possible. The impossible is known as the affirmation of a thing together with its negation, the affirmation of the more specific together with the negation of the more general, and the affirmation of two together with the negation of one. He said: Whatever does not return to that is possible, so a world more wondrous than this world enters into it. And Allah is the Granter of success to what He wills.

Since man, despite these excellences, has been subjected by God, glory be to Him and exalted, to appetites, and He has disposed his nature toward base vices and vile characters, and toward desires and personal pleasures that incline him away, and since most of creation perishes through them, so that God's power may become manifest, He made no exception but passed judgment on the whole species through them, just as He passed judgment on it with (the perfection of) stature. Therefore He, exalted, said, using the particle of delay (*thumma*, "then") to indicate that his deviation after that sound intellect and clear, illuminated mind is extremely remote, were it not for the overwhelming power and the compelling, dominating force: ﴿Then We returned him﴾, that is, by what We possess of complete power and all-encompassing knowledge, so that he nullified the benefits of what We created him for, wasted his own self, and forfeited the means of his happiness. And We reversed him in His creation, so that by both matters he became, in his character and in his form, a self and a desire, or more general than that (p-143) by the reversal, ﴿to the lowest of the low﴾, that is, to a rank below that of the repulsive inanimate things. Thus he began to do evil deeds, which necessarily follow, after the goodness of the combination, into utter dispersion.

As for His returning him in his character, it is that We subjected him to the appetites which We composed within souls and made into callers to every misery. They overpowered his intellect and blinded it until they brought him to the watering places and cast him into ruin and destruction, to the extent that he rides many of his affairs while certain that they are a shameful falsehood, which no intelligent person would undertake. Thus he worships, besides God, what is below the human being, indeed what is merely animal, of which there is neither harm nor benefit. He comes to ride oppression, transgression, falsehood, and calumny, and countless kinds of indecencies and disobedience. He wrongs his own kind and others, strives in corruption, and conducts himself in ways he himself does not doubt that no one with even slight insight would allow, from among those who have authority over his affairs and who concern themselves with his condition. Thus he becomes lower in rank than the beasts, indeed than the lowest of repulsive insects, because although they have appetites, they have no intellect with which to conceal and extinguish its light with their darkness. Hence they are not charged with having wasted anything, since they are not under obligation, lacking the intellect that entails honor. But he has used the faculties that We created for him and the perfections with which We distinguished him for other than what We created them for, and so he deserved the humiliating punishment. Then he dies without being recompensed for any of that, or for much of it. Therefore wisdom necessarily requires his resurrection, and after the resurrection there is for him, with his Lord, an enduring punishment for that.

As for His returning him in his form, it is by senility, until after those powers he becomes weak, and after that might he becomes humbled and abased, and after that vast knowledge and luminous thought he knows nothing, and those who used to be fond of him and perfume themselves for him come to loathe him and reject him.

Ibn Burjan said: As for His returning him in the path of religion, it is by disbelief and denial. As for what pertains to recompense, it is by transformation in the realm of the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection) and the changing of his form into that which his nature and deeds in this world made dominant, namely beasts, creeping things, and animals. In the Hereafter his eyes will turn blue and his creation will be disfigured.

Abu al-'Abbas al-Iqlishi said in his commentary on *al-Muqaddam al-Mu'akhkhar* from his commentary on *al-Sama' al-Husna* (the Most Beautiful Names): Indeed God, exalted, created him—

that is, man—first in the best of stature, then assembled him in this body, which draws him down to the lowest of the low. If he gives precedence to his intellect over his desire, he ascends to the highest of the high ('Illiyyin), and is among those brought near and given precedence. If he gives precedence to his desire, he descends to the reaches of the Blazing Fire, and is among those removed and placed last.

(p-145) When He had passed this judgment of reversion upon the whole human species, indicating that many of them would be characterized by it, and since the righteous were very few, He made them the object of the exception, saying: ﴿Except those who believe﴾, that is, in God and His messengers, so they were among those possessed of insight and knowledge. We overcame their intellects with Our subtle grace, by that to which the primordial nature (al-fitrah al-ula) called and which it helped them against their desires. We preserved them from the lowest state of life. So whenever We increased them in years, We increased the lights of their intellects and diminished the fire of their desires, by weakening the firmness of their natures and their attachment to this world, and by strengthening in them the faculties for perceiving the lights of the Truth and its illuminations, and by magnifying the powers of their spirits.

Since a person may claim faith falsely, He said: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, that is, as confirmation of their claim of faith, ﴿righteous deeds﴾, that is, of the finest good deeds, both of speech and action, firmly rooted on the foundation of faith, perfected by the knowledge We gave them to the utmost degree of perfection, and mastered to the utmost degree of mastery. For We preserved them — and few are they — by what We perfected them with and honored them above all animals and all others besides them. We did not empower desires or anything else over them, and We established them upon what the method of reason requires. So they followed the messengers, because We kept them upon the primordial nature in the best of forms, which was not defiled in its face by lust, nor by self-interest, nor by whim. Thus their submission was easy, and that led them to justice (p-146), equity, goodness, all noble character and lofty matters, and they did not deviate from the method of the messengers in word or deed.

The verse, as you see, is of the type of *ihtibak* (concealment through mutual reference): first, the mention of the doing of evil deeds was omitted, being understood from the verse; and second, the retention of the origin of creation in the best of forms upon the primordial nature was omitted. Its original arrangement would be: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 5] through doing evil deeds, so for him there is a humiliating punishment for that; ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for We kept them upon the primordial nature in the best of forms.

Since the context is one of praising the believers, it was fitting to mention their deeds by which they earned favor as a cause, just as the reward was bestowed upon them as a favor. So He said: ﴿For them﴾, that is, it follows from that, for them in both abodes, in accordance with what they were granted success in, of what pleases Him, glorified and exalted be He, ﴿is a reward﴾, that is, a very great one, and it is, along with that, ﴿unending﴾, that is, uncut off, or one that He does not hold over them as a favor even in the state of illness and decrepitude, because they strove for the pleasure of God, glorified and exalted be He, and resolved with a sincere resolve that they would not be diminished in acts of righteousness by an atom even if they lived through the span of time. That reward is a recompense for their deeds, a bounty from Him in origin and in branch, to the extent that when they become incapable through old age, He records for them the reward of what they used to do in the state of health. And for those who follow their desire in descent there is a great punishment, because they were returned to the lowest of the low.

(p-147) Since it has been established by this that it is not permissible in wisdom to leave them without recompense, given what is observed of some of them oppressing others, in defiance of what sound reason, about which there is no doubt, requires, it follows that this is such that no one among them would approve of it, and no creature would allow slaves in his dominion to act this way toward one another, with some of them transgressing against others and him leaving them alone. Rather, he must either restrain them from one another or take from the wrongdoer on behalf of the wronged. Even if that owner were the least and most ignorant of people, how much more so if he were intelligent, how much more so if he were a ruler, how much more so if he feared no one, how much more so if he were just and equitable, and the comprehensiveness of his knowledge and power, glory be to Him and exalted, has been established. It is entirely good that this should be a reason for denouncing those who suppose that God leaves His servants without judgment between them, so that each of the obedient and the disobedient may be repaid for what he did, given what you see of some of them oppressing others, and that the wrongdoer may die before retaliation. So He said, as a consequence of the promise, as expressed by the Scriptures, of reward for the believers, whom oppressors have long transgressed against, and whom wicked people have deprived of their rights, and as a threat, as implied by the address, for the criminals who have long transgressed against others: ﴿So what﴾, that is, as a consequence of establishing the proof of complete power and of slaves transgressing against one another, it is said to you, confirming what you reported (p-148) that God, glory be to Him and exalted, will resurrect creatures after their death in order to repay each for what he did, and as a denunciation of whoever denies you: ﴿what denies you﴾, that is, what thing attributes falsehood to you, O noblest of creation, most perfect in soul, most pure in honor, and purest in form and character? He used "what" (mā) to indicate that denying this, together with this decisive proof contained in this surah, is among what is not rational, rather is even lower than that, ﴿after this﴾, that is, after witnessing some people transgressing against others, employing the state of reversal, and he removed the preposition from it to indicate that whoever believes before the death rattle and whose faith continues up to his death, is among those who have an unending reward. ﴿by the Judgment﴾, that is, the recompense for each person according to what he deserves, in the way of justice and equity, on account of those deeds in which desires overcame intellects, so that there occurred by them such wrongdoing and harm that no rational servant could regard as good the leaving of their doer without recompense, to the point that most of the deeds of servants are wrongdoing. And it is the way of kings to be equitable among their slaves and subjects, so how much more so is God, glory be to Him and exalted, who has legislated that for His servants, and who, by His great character, and by this firmly ordered system and most upright method, has been established as the Wise, with none wise besides Him, the Knowing, with none knowing besides Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 95, verse 8:

(p-149) Since it is established that one who leaves the wrongdoer unpunished and the doer of good without honor is not upon the path of justice (*'adl*) that God has legislated, the repetition of the rebuke in His words, glorified and exalted be He, is very fitting: ﴿Is not God﴾, i.e., with all the attributes of perfection that belong to Him. He emphasized it with the prepositional phrase in His words: ﴿the most just of judges﴾, i.e., so that He would not leave the creatures to destroy one another without recompense, which would make their creation vain. Rather, He is the most judicious of judges in knowledge, power, justice and wisdom, as witnessed in His originating of creation and the variety He placed among them, and in His making the human being among them in the best stature. Therefore He must establish recompense and set the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, so that His justice, wisdom and bounty become manifest. This last is first in terms of the prophethood through which His judgment and wisdom became manifest, and it is the thing sworn to, since the creation in the best stature necessarily requires justice, and the return to the lowest of the low necessarily requires judgments because of the injustice and strife that occur between those who remained upon the upright nature and those who were returned to the lowest of the low. This surah, despite its brevity, has comprised in summary all the aims of the Torah, and it added indication of the Hereafter. Its oath corresponds to His saying in the Torah: "The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto us, and shined forth from Mount Paran." The creation in [the best] stature is the creation of Adam (p-150), peace be upon him, mentioned at its beginning, and the creation of his spouse and what they need from the heaven and the earth, and the creation of the chosen ones from their offspring and what they brought of good. Those who believed and did righteous deeds are what it contains of the laws and rulings. His saying, after what preceded of the one referred to by the oath: "With him are ten thousands of the holy ones at his right hand; he gave them and loved the peoples, and blessed all his holy ones," and the return to the lowest of the low is what it mentioned at its beginning of the disobedient, from Cain and those after him to its end, as indicated by the disobedience of the Children of Israel that made them deserving of the curse. So it encompassed the beginning, middle and end of the Torah. It began with its end because it concerns the prophethood, which is the most important of the important matters, since it is the means of salvation from the evil of highway robbers. Its end is the most indicative in it of the prophethood, especially the three great [...] referred to by the oath of this surah. And God, glorified and exalted be He, knows best the unseen.
